fact: The Minister of Economy, Commerce, Industry and Digital Transition held a strategic consultation in Praia on 6 August 2026 whose contributions are to deepen the national diagnosis and support the priorities and measures of the future digital transformation agenda, which the document describes as cross-government and not yet written.

On 6 August 2026 the government convened public administration, private sector, academia and experts in a consultation on digital transformation (interoperability, service digitisation, skills, innovation, inclusion, data protection, cybersecurity) to feed the future agenda.

The Council of Ministers approved Resolução n.º 72/2026, establishing the strategic bases for the Agenda Digital de Cabo Verde 2035, an instrument across economic development, digital government, social inclusion, environmental sustainability, smart cities and fintech (Expresso das Ilhas, 8 May 2026; the approval date is not given, so the publication date is used).

The Agenda Digital 2035 names the Comissão Nacional da Estratégia Digital, whose operationalisation is one of its enabling pillars, and states that progress will be monitored by the Observatório da Sociedade da Informação.
The government approved Resolução n.º 72/2026 on the Agenda Digital 2035 in the Council of Ministers, reported on 8 May 2026 (the approval date is not given, so the publication date is used).

At the third ordinary meeting of the Conselho Consultivo da Economia Digital on 25 November 2025, chaired by the Vice-Prime Minister, the Estratégia da Economia Digital de Cabo Verde, which the document says guides the country's transformation into a platform country, was presented to the council; the document does not say it was adopted.

fact: The AfDB appraisal report of October 2022 cites the Cabo Verde Digital Agenda 2019-21, under which the Government set strategies for connectivity, capacity building, service provision and governance, as a strategy of the period 2019-2021; the report is dated after that period and does not say whether a successor exists (the document's published date is used for the as-at).

The environmental and social impact study states that the General Directorate of Telecommunications and Digital Economy (DGTED) is tasked with formulating the country's digital strategy, with government sectors, regulators, research bodies, companies and civil society, and that the Ministry of the Digital Economy supports the development and implementation of Cape Verde's Digital Strategy; no finance is stated, and the document gives no date for these mandates other than its own, August 2022.

NOSi's 2019-2022 action plan states that implementation of the Estratégia para a Economia Digital (connectivity hub, capacity-building hub, service-provision hub) is under way under the Government programme with African Development Bank and World Bank support; it gives no results against the strategy's targets (the document gives no date for the statement, so its published date of March 2020 is used).
